sentences.text: Daohugoupterus is a genus of pterosaur found in the Middle to Late Jurassic Daohugou Beds of the Tiaojishan Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
It is a small pterosaur with a humerus measuring 41.8 mm in length.

The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — includes parts of the torso, pectoral girdle, left humerus, coracoids, scapula, sternal plate, vertebrae, ribs, and the posterior skull and lower jaws.
Two distinguishing traits considered possible autapomorphies are the nasal bones deeply invading the frontal bones and a sternal plate that is 2.5 times wider than it is long.
Daohugoupterus is a member of the Yanliao Biota and is the smallest of the three pterosaurs in that group, along with Jeholopterus and Pterorhynchus.
Daohugoupterus was named and described in 2015 by Cheng Xin, Wang Xiaolin, Jiang Shunxing, and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner.

The holotype specimen was acquired by the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology at Beijing through field work by Zhou Zhonghe and Li Yan at the village of Daohugou near Linglongta.
Features such as short neck vertebrae, cervical ribs, and a quadrangular deltopectoral crest indicate Daohugoupterus was a relatively basal pterosaur outside the Pterodactyloidea.
Daohugoupterus is classified as Pterosauria incertae sedis.
Daohugoupterus lived during the Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
